newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank urges holders to reject pay cap.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank urges holders to reject pay cap.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada's top executives took home fatter pay packets in 1996, the bank said on Thursday as it urged shareholders to reject an activist's proposals on limiting senior pay.
The top earner among Royal Bank's senior executives was Anthony Fell, chairman and chief executive of the bank's brokerage arm, RBC Dominion Securities.

Fell's pay packet soared to C$4.8 million in 1996 from C$2 million the year earlier. Royal Bank chairman and chief executive John Cleghorn earned C$2.1 million last year, up from C$1.8 million in 1995.
The compensation data were included in Royal Bank's management proxy circular mailed out to shareholders for its annual meeting on March 5 in Vancouver.

The circular also included several proposals from shareholder activist Yves Michaud who won a Quebec court ruling earlier this month forcing Royal and National Bank of Canada to put his proposals to a vote.

Michaud has called for limiting executives' pay to 20 times that of an average bank employee, limiting director's tenure, restricting who can become a bank director and preventing bank executives from becoming chairman.
"Management opposes these proposals or the reasons set out after each of them," Royal Bank said in its circular.
On the compensation issue, the bank said it must offer competitive pay packets to attract and keep "highly skilled and motivated executives."
Royal Bank said its compensation policy was set at a level comparable to the top 25 percent of the country's largest corporations and financial institutions.
